KARANDEEP SALUJA
AI/ML Engineer
Greater Noida, India

SUMMARY
Five years building production machine learning systems, the last two focused on
real-time voice agents and applied LLM work. Comfortable owning a problem from
data collection through to a deployed service, and used to being the person a
client asks why a model behaves the way it does.

EXPERIENCE

AI/ML Engineer
Appinventiv, Noida
2023 to present

Voice agents

- Built six production voice agents on LiveKit Agents with OpenAI Realtime,
  covering drive-thru ordering, home services booking, hotel concierge and
  patient appointment booking. Deployed on a shared Ubuntu VM under systemd.
- Established a pattern now used across all voice work: safety guardrails belong
  in code, not prompts. Prompt-level rules failed five out of five live attempts
  on emergency routing; the same rules enforced in Python held at 100 percent.
- Moved four guardrails out of prompts and into code on a medical booking agent:
  emergency state persistence, patient identity enforcement, exact-match alias
  resolution, and child-to-paediatrics routing.
- Diagnosed a stutter in the drive-thru agent as a prompt contradiction causing
  hidden model deliberation, not a latency problem. Fixed by letting the order
  tool accept item lists rather than one item per call.
- Rebuilt a 163-row menu from a raw export to support per-service pricing and
  availability across dine-in, pickup and delivery, with cart flushing on
  service switch.

Model fine-tuning and MLOps

- Replaced GPT-4o with a fine-tuned Sarvam-M 24B for a health-tech tool call
  classifier. bf16 LoRA on SageMaker ml.g7e.2xlarge, 914 training examples, and
  a custom Mistral-format jinja template for tool calls.
- Reached 97.08 percent decision accuracy against the GPT-4o reference ceiling.
- Quantised to GPTQ 4-bit at 14.2 GB with statistically flat accuracy against
  the bf16 baseline.
- Replaced a YOLO pipeline with Qwen3-VL-4B for seven-segment display OCR on
  medical devices, taking accuracy from 90 to 97 percent.

Speech and audio

- Built an audio language identification prototype: VoxLingua107 ECAPA ensembled
  with Whisper-small, with IndicConformer as the downstream ASR.
- Benchmarked on FLEURS across seven Indian languages. Bengali and English at
  100 percent, Gujarati 90, Tamil and Marathi 70. Hindi and Urdu confused
  bidirectionally, which is a real limitation of the acoustic signal rather than
  a tuning problem.
- Traced an apparent silence-detection failure to lead-in silence in the
  benchmark clips rather than the model, and fixed it with RMS normalisation.

Computer vision

- Ran a defect detection proof of concept for a jewellery manufacturer.
  PatchCore anomaly detection validated for solder cut defects.
- Reported that the prong-open detector reached roughly 0.50 AUROC, which is
  chance, because inspector markup had been drawn directly over the defect
  pixels. Recommended the client fix the labelling process rather than tune the
  number upward.

Platform and observability

- Built the observability stack for an internal AI governance platform: OTel
  Collector into Tempo, Prometheus, Loki and Grafana, with Langfuse for LLM
  traces and Metabase for reporting on a read-only role.
- Made model registration durable with a Postgres catalog and boot hydration,
  proving restart survival.
- Established that model comparison must join on exact model reference, after
  demonstrating that prefix matching made gpt-4o silently include gpt-4o-mini
  traffic.

Retrieval and chatbots

- Added a lab-test booking agent stack to a live FastAPI health chatbot without
  modifying a single line of the two existing versions.
- Fixed an intent classifier that was routing five diagnostics queries to the
  wrong handler. 76 of 76 test cases passing afterwards.

ML Engineer
Previous role, Delhi NCR
2021 to 2023

- Built and maintained an inherited FastAPI service on SQS, Bedrock and MongoDB,
  taking sole ownership after handover.
- Produced the runbook the team still uses, after finding that CI auto-deployed
  only two of the four environments and the rest were handled elsewhere.
